what: a 9 mm chamfer on the top front edge of a cube with square openings 5 mm in runs past the 5 mm between the edge and the openings: built as if the faces went on over the openings, then cut by them (cliff overflow); it never bridges an opening
method: cube 20 less three orthogonal 10x10 through openings (cross): V0 = 4000. The chamfer plane takes, of the section, the triangle y + (20 - z) <= 9 (y >= 0, z <= 20), area 40.5, along x: 810; less its parts inside the openings: the x opening (y, z in [5, 15]) misses it (z >= 11 + y >= 16 there), the y opening (z in [5, 15], x in [5, 15]) holds y in [0, 4], z in [11 + y, 15]: area 8, times 10 = 80, the z opening (y in [5, 15], x in [5, 15]) holds y in [5, 9], z in [11 + y, 20]: area 8, times 10 = 80. V = 4000 - (810 - 160) = 3350.
